transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Priya (PM), Mateo (Eng Lead), Linh (SRE), Jordan (Prod Ops), Anita (QA), Ethan (Infra), Annie (VP Product), Devon (Head of Platform)

AUTO-GENERATED SUMMARY (may be imperfect):
- Retro on recent private deploy pilot and incident escalations; gap analysis for launch gating.
- Agreed on concrete gating criteria (latency p95, error rates, KV cache hit ratio) and owners.
- Next steps: run staging scale test, produce rollback runbook, finalize test matrix, schedule canary.

TOPICS:
1) Quick retro: pilot incidents and root causes
2) Launch gating checklist and SLO thresholds
3) Canary plan and on-call rotations
4) Security/KMS flow for private deployments
5) QA/regression and postmortem comms

[00:00] Priya: ok, uh, kick off — thanks everyone for joining, I know it's a busy week. Let's do a 60 minute sync, retrospective first on the private-deploy pilot, then we gotta lock the gating checklist for Q4 launch.
[00:18] Mateo: yeah, I'll jump in with the incident summary, I pulled the postmortem notes into the deck — small caveat, transcription might scramble some names.
[00:28] Linh: real quick, I also pushed the extra logs to the shared s3 bucket, link in the notes. There were two spikes that matched a KV cache thrash behavior.
[00:40] Mateo: right — incident A on 08/09: latency jumps p95 from 120ms to 3.2s for a 12 minute window, increase in load + cache invalidations, and then incident B where autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough for sustained tails.
[01:00] Anita: and from QA's side, we had a missed regression where the batching config change altered token chunking and caused a small percentage of malformed outputs. We caught it in canary but it leaked in pilot because the canary wasn't covering the embedded model variant.
[01:20] Jordan: so two categories — runtime scaling and batching/config compatibility. We need explicit compatibility matrix in the gating checklist.
[01:33] Priya: agreed. Let's enumerate gating criteria now. I want owners and thresholds. Mateo, start us off with performance SLOs.
[01:42] Mateo: baseline for private deploy launch: p50 <= 90ms, p95 <= 200ms for small seq workloads (<=128), p95 <= 400ms for medium seq (<=512). Error budget set at 0.5% 5xx per 24hr window. Also KV cache hit rate target >= 85% for steady-state.
[02:05] Linh: we should add a cold-start / warm cache metric — 99th percentile cold start under 1s. And autoscaler convergence time < 45s for expected scale events.
[02:20] Ethan: on infra side, note that for private deploys KMS key rotations add jitter; validated rotation path shows up to 800ms added for a subset of requests, so include KMS latency in SLO tests.
[02:35] Priya: good call. Anita, QA gating?
[02:40] Anita: must-have test categories: e2e inference correctness on representative prompts, regression pack across quantization levels, load tests at 3x expected traffic, meltdown tests (disk/IO and network flakiness). Blocker if malformed outputs > 0.1% or if deviation vs baseline quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/SBERT cosine) exceeds threshold.
[03:05] Annie (VP Product): add product acceptance — UX signal that fallbacks work gracefully (e.g., returning shorter responses vs 500s). We don't want customer-visible errors.
[03:20] Devon: also compliance: ensure audit logs show key management operations and access events for private deploy control plane. Need SSO (SAML) smoke test.

--- Discussion / Retro: root cause, mitigations ---
[04:00] Mateo: root cause summary: caching churn + a packing config optimization we shipped that changed continuous batching heuristics; combined produced heavier per-request CPU and more tail latency. The autoscaler threshold was tuned assuming old packing.
[04:25] Linh: mitigation that helped during the pilot was temporary: reduced concurrency per worker and increased batch timeout which reduced malformed outputs but increased p50 a bit. Not sustainable.
[04:40] Anita: QA missed the quantized path because our test harness defaulted to fp16. We need matrix coverage automated.
[04:52] Priya: so action items — (1) freeze packing heuristics for launch unless proven otherwise, (2) add packing-specific tests to CI, (3) adjust autoscaler tuning and add predictive scale ramp for warm-ups.
[05:10] Mateo: on predictive scaling — we can seed KV cache via a prefix warmup during deployment to avoid the cold spike. That adds ops steps but reduces tail.
[05:25] Ethan: we have a tool to pre-warm caches in dedicated pools, but for private we need a tenant-aware warmup. I'll prototype a tenant-warmup script and share.
[05:40] Jordan: canary plan — propose staggered canary: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with health checks at each stage for 30 minutes. If p95 breach or error rate > 0.5% revert. Need on-call coverage for 24 hours post 50% stage.
[06:05] Priya: sounds reasonable. Let's commit to health-check gating and an automated rollback if certain thresholds happen. Mateo will own the automated rollback toggle.
[06:18] Mateo: got it. We'll implement a canary supervisor that will flip traffic via routing policy and call the fallback model when necessary. We'll expose a kill-switch.

[06:35] Linh: question on private deploy network topologies — do we require customers to run a sidecar for KV caching or integrate with their existing Redis? This changes our warmup story.
[06:48] Priya: for the Q4 GA we want two supported modes: managed Redis sidecar packaged with deployment, and external Redis with clear config. Document recommended sizing.
[06:59] Devon: for security gating: KMS path must be verified, SAML assertions validated; we need an internal checklist item for pen-test signoff before GA. Also legal asked for data retention clarifications.
[07:20] Priya: include a compliance checkbox: SOC2 scoping for private deploy — make sure audit events are available to customer and to us for control plane actions.

[07:38] Anita: test matrix detail — I propose automated jobs: nightly regression across models, quantization variants, and a weekly canary run in staging that simulates spikes. Failure criteria baked into CI and bubble up to Slack #prod-gates.
[07:58] Mateo: make sure to tag tests to the release branch and gate merges. We'll also require that any packing change has a perf bench result attached.

[08:10] Priya: okay time for questions and edge cases.
[08:15] Ethan: edge case — network partition between control plane and private node; we saw weird behavior where model kept serving stale KV because the control plane couldn't commit deletes. Need clear eventual-consistency semantics in doc.
[08:30] Mateo: add in the docs: KV operations are best-effort with last-write-wins; for critical revocations we must push invalidation tokens to nodes with immediate effect via out-of-band.
[08:44] Priya: note that as a launch blocker: token revocation for data residency must be demonstrable in under X minutes — assign to Ethan to validate.

[09:00] Jordan: comms & postmortem strategy — if we hit a degraded canary during GA we should have a pre-approved customer-facing message and a private incident template. Annie to own customer comms.
[09:14] Annie: yep I'll prep the templates and sync with legal.

--- Mid-call check: 30 minute mark, we review progress ---
[30:02] Priya: we're halfway, quick recap of owners, then deep-dive into the onboarding runbook.
[30:15] Mateo: runbook items: deploy steps, migration of model weights, quantization hooks, kernel selection flags, and rollback steps with traffic shift commands. I'll publish a runbook draft to GH rwd-private-deploy/runbooks.
[30:32] Linh: include troubleshooting matrix: high cpu, OOM on GPU, socket timeouts, KMS timeouts. Each with primary/backup remediation.
[30:45] Anita: test hooks in runbook for smoke tests post-deploy — sample prompts, tokenization sanity checks, and latency smoke.
[30:55] Ethan: infra checklist: kube distro version, driver versions, nvlib compatibility, and secure kubelet config. We should pin recommended kernel and driver matrix for private customers.

[31:10] Mateo: one tricky item — quantized kernels differ per hardware; we need a minimal verified matrix of model + quantization + driver combos. This will be an ongoing maintenance item.
[31:25] Priya: ok, for launch gating we'll require that supported stacks have at least one verified config and a list of known unsupported combos.

[31:40] Jordan: on the rollout — propose that Dedicated customers get an opt-in longer validation window. Private GA by invite only initially.
[31:52] Annie: agree, phased rollout reduces blast radius. Also tie early access to committed capacity/contracts where appropriate.

--- Security/KMS break-out ---
[38:05] Ethan: dug into KMS rotation: we measured worst-case latency spike on rotate events when keys are reauthorized. For private, recommend scheduled rotation windows and a pre-warm path that refreshes cached tokens.
[38:28] Devon: legal/security wants proof-of-concept that we never persist plaintext keys and that audit logs are tamper-evident. We'll need a short security note for enterprise teams.
[38:45] Priya: add that as a checklist item — security note + SAML smoke.

--- QA / E2E specifics ---
[42:00] Anita: on malformed outputs: we need golden prompts that exercise edge-case tokenization and structured output. Also a metric for drift in generation quality that triggers a human review.
[42:20] Mateo: can we use pairwise compare vs baseline using embedding cosine and a threshold? If the delta > 0.08 we flag. We used that internally last quarter.
[42:34] Anita: fine, put that into test harness and export daily deltas to the dashboard.

--- Closing / Recap ---
[55:40] Priya: wrap up — recap of owners and deadlines: Priya finalize gating doc 8/24, Mateo runbook + rollback 8/26, Linh staging scale test 8/28, Anita regression pack 8/27, Ethan KMS validation 8/25. Annie will prepare comms templates.
[55:58] Devon: reminder: we need a one pager for legal on data retention and audit events by 8/25.
[56:10] Priya: schedule wise — targeted canary 9/02; will set calendar and invite on-call. If all green, GA in mid-late September after contract and security signoffs.
[56:25] Mateo: quick note — add a telemetry tag to canary traffic so we can filter metrics easily.
[56:33] Linh: and require a prepared dashboard with p50/p95, errors, KV hitrate before we start canary.

[56:50] Priya: final Qs?
[56:55] Anita: none from me, but please ping QA channel for any last-minute model changes.
[57:03] Mateo: also — to avoid last-minute surprises we should freeze non-critical runtime changes 72 hours before canary.
[57:10] Priya: freeze noted.

[57:20] Priya: thanks everyone. I'll circulate notes and the gating checklist link. We'll reconvene next week if there are blockers.
